q1_who.name: q1_who
q1_who.value: Sandro is an accessible-luxury Parisian ready-to-wear house (founded 1984 by Evelyne Chetrite, who still provides creative direction) and the largest brand within SMCP Group, alongside Maje, Claudie Pierlot and Fursac. Tier: accessible-luxury — live PDPs show full-price points of ~$300–480 (e.g. $480 knit dress, $315 polo). Channel mix is DTC-led (own eshops across many country/market sites: US, FR, etc.) plus selective wholesale and marketplace partners; the group runs a strict full-price strategy. SMCP is a global accessible-luxury leader present in 59 countries with 1,600+ stores; the group is listed on Euronext Paris (ticker SMCP).

q2_direction.name: q2_direction
q2_direction.value: AHEAD ON CRAFT — lead with consistency, not innovation-for-its-own-sake. Wayback then-vs-now shows Sandro has run a tightly art-directed, on-model studio house look for years: the 2022 snapshot already presents a polished seasonal-collection eshop (titled "Fall/Winter 2021 Collection"), and the live 2026 PDPs show the same disciplined studio-grey on-model + still-life + per-PDP video standard. So the brand is not visually behind and does not need a new creative direction — the opening is protecting that hard-won consistency across channels (off-brand wholesale/marketplace imagery is markdown risk), not proposing reinvention. No new-creative-director/rebrand/replatform trigger observed; platform remains Salesforce Commerce Cloud (demandware).

q3_momentum.name: q3_momentum
q3_momentum.value: RECOVERING (with a SPLIT nuance to flag). SMCP Group returned to profit in FY2025: sales €1,217.4m (+1.7% organic), net income €17m (a +€40m swing from −€24m in 2024), adjusted EBIT €95m (+80%, 7.8% margin), record free cash flow €91m and net debt cut 38% to €148m. Strict full-price strategy (in-season discount down to ~20%). SPLIT nuance: France (core market, ~€411m) was DOWN 1.6% organically with a weak H2 amid political/social uncertainty, while EMEA-ex-France and the Americas drove growth; and ownership is in flux (results note potential costs tied to "a potential capital transaction at SMCP" / disputed DTG–ETS stake). Sandro-brand-specific revenue (~€609m) is an estimate, not separately disclosed in these results — flagged for human verification.

q5_pdp.name: q5_pdp

Classified mix across the sample: ~60% on-model, ~30% still-life/packshot, plus flat-lay/detail and per-PDP video. Art direction is highly consistent — uniform studio-grey backgrounds, same framing and model-styling language across categories. Consistency IS the brand asset on Sandro's own DTC. The exposure is cross-channel: wholesale and marketplace partners frequently show downgraded or off-brand imagery, breaking that fidelity (concrete, demoable pain). Platform: Salesforce Commerce Cloud (demandware) across localized country eshops.

strategy.name: strategy
strategy.value: Win it consistency-first, group-wide. Lead with brand-consistent, garment-accurate on-model + still-life imagery held to Sandro's standard across DTC, wholesale, marketplace and localized markets; make price the second sentence, never the first — framed as ROI/efficiency without quality loss, matching SMCP's FY2025 profit-and-cash turnaround (EBIT +80%, record €91m FCF). Sell one relationship across all four SMCP brands (Sandro, Maje, Claudie Pierlot, Fursac) to size the partner upside, not the single brand. Quantify the localization lever explicitly — localized imagery at near-zero marginal cost across SMCP's 59-country eshop footprint is a concrete number to put on the table. Do NOT pitch reinvention: there is no new-CD/rebrand/replatform trigger and the brand is already ahead on craft — the play is protecting hard-won consistency, not proposing a new look.
